PhD studies
På svenska
The PhD programme at the Centre for Mathematical Sciences at Lund University offers the opportunity to undertake advanced studies in mathematics, mathematical statistics and their applications at the forefront of modern mathematics.
A PhD post at the Centre for Mathematical Sciences usually lasts for 5 years, 20 per cent of which is devoted to departmental duties, such as teaching. The remainder of the time is spent taking courses and working on your own research project. Upon completion of the PhD programme, you will be awarded a doctoral degree, which opens up opportunities for a career in academia or in the business sector. The Centre for Mathematical Sciences is shared between LTH (Faculty of Engineering) and the Faculty of Science, and PhD students are employed by their respective faculties.
This page contains information about the PhD programme at the Centre for Mathematical Sciences for current PhD students and for those interested in pursuing PhD studies.
General information
Study plans
The Centre for Mathematical Sciences has PhD students from both LTH (Faculty of Engineering) and the Faculty of Science. The PhD programme follows general study plans.
